text:
alex: Quick q — running into a weird Host header + SNI issue when using our Go SDK against a VPC private endpoint through an HTTP proxy. I set baseURL to https://private.redwood.internal and proxy to http://proxy.corp.local, but upstream sees Host: proxy.corp.local and TLS SNI != private.redwood.internal. Any proven workarounds? cc @mira @jordan_t

mira: If you're doing an HTTP CONNECT tunnel the Host header should be the upstream host normally, but some proxy setups / libs rewrite it. Which Go version and transport config are you using?

alex: Go 1.20, using net/http with a custom Transport: `transport := &http.Transport{Proxy: http.ProxyURL(proxyURL), TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{}, ...}`. When streaming responses I sometimes get 407s and SNI ends up as the proxy host. Minimal repro logs: `CONNECT private.redwood.internal:443 HTTP/1.1`, then the TLS handshake appears to use proxy host as SNI.

jordan_t: 407 suggests proxy auth issues too, but the SNI/Host mix looks like the request Host is being set to the proxy host somewhere. Are you setting `req.Host` anywhere? In Go, if `req.Host` is non-empty it overrides the Host header used for the request. Try `req.Host = ""` before `client.Do(req)`. Also ensure `req.URL.Host` stays the upstream host.

sam_k: Another gotcha: if you set headers like `req.Header.Set("Host", ...)` that will be used. For CONNECT the proxy should only see the absolute host in the CONNECT line; SNI is set by the client's TLS config. Make sure you set `TLSClientConfig.ServerName = "private.redwood.internal"` if autopicked SNI is wrong.

mira: For our internal VPC endpoints we've seen proxies that rewrite CONNECT or do TLS interception (corporate TLS proxies). Confirm whether your proxy is a transparent MITM vs a pure tunnel. If it's a tunnel, Go will use the actual TLS handshake to the upstream host. If it's a terminating proxy, SNI will be proxy's.

alex: I'm not setting req.Host explicitly. I did try `Transport.ProxyConnectHeader` for Proxy-Authorization but not ServerName. Example change I tried: ```go
req.Host = ""
transport.TLSClientConfig = &tls.Config{ServerName: "private.redwood.internal"}
client := &http.Client{Transport: transport}
resp, err := client.Do(req)
```

mira: That looks right. Also consider setting `transport.ProxyConnectHeader = http.Header{"Proxy-Authorization": []string{"Basic ..."}}` instead of adding auth to each req header; that ensures auth is sent during CONNECT. For streaming, `Transport.MaxIdleConnsPerHost` and `ResponseHeaderTimeout` helped us with chunking issues.

jordan_t: I'll add a small SDK example to the repo demonstrating a proxied CONNECT with explicit `TLSClientConfig.ServerName` and clearing `req.Host`. Also include a note about corporate TLS proxies. I'll claim PR-789 for that. @alex can you review when I push it?

alex: One other question: when using mTLS (client cert) and a proxy in the middle, does the client cert go to the proxy or the upstream? I assume only to upstream (after CONNECT), so the proxy never gets the cert. Correct?

sam_k: Correct — client cert is presented in the TLS handshake to the upstream server after the CONNECT tunnel is established. Proxy only sees the outer CONNECT request and can challenge auth for the tunnel, but not the downstream client cert unless it terminates TLS.

alex: Thanks — I'll try setting `req.Host = ""`, set ServerName, and move proxy auth into `ProxyConnectHeader`. Quick update later. thx :thumbsup:

(alex later): Update — clearing `req.Host` + `TLSClientConfig.ServerName` fixed SNI mismatch. Adding `ProxyConnectHeader` solved the 407s. Streaming still had occasional truncated chunks; setting `transport.MaxIdleConnsPerHost = 100`, `transport.ResponseHeaderTimeout = 15*time.Second`, and `transport.DisableKeepAlives = false` reduced those. I'll open a PR with a reproducible example and notes about corporate TLS proxies.

mira: Nice! Please include a tiny section about when a proxy terminates TLS vs tunnels, and how that affects mTLS and Host/SNI.

jordan_t: PR-802 created, adding the example and tests. Assigning review to @mira and @alex.

devex-bot: PR-802 is linked to issue #456 (docs: proxied private endpoints) and added to the 2-week sprint backlog.

mira: Thanks everyone. Adding doc task to the SDK quickstarts. :rocket:
